_읽는이에게: 검색창 대신 이걸 만든 이유 (2026-08-16 운영자 제안 → 검토):
그리고 32편에서 검색창을 달면 Jeju·DMZ·hiking 이 전부 0건으로 나온다.
지금은 얇다는 게 안 보이는데, 검색창은 그걸 독자가 측정하게 만든다.
→ 우리가 먼저 보여준다. 80편쯤에서 Pagefind 로 검색을 넣는다.
① when 은 **독자의 말**로 적는다. 우리 제목을 줄인 게 아니라
그 사람이 그 순간에 머릿속으로 하는 말이어야 한다.
② answer 는 **한 문장으로 실제 답을 준다.** 미끼가 아니다.
클릭 안 해도 도움이 되어야 한다. 그게 검색창이 못 하는 일이다.
③ answer 는 반드시 그 기사 안에 있는 사실이어야 한다.
확정 못 한 숫자는 여기 쓰지 않는다 (진료비가 그래서 범위 없이 적혀 있다).
href 가 실제 기사와 맞지 않으면 **빌드가 선다.** StuckIndex.astro 가 막는다.
쓰지 않은 문제는 여기 올리지 않는다 — 없는 답을 약속하는 목록이 된다.

items.when: I am at the airport and do not know how to get into the city
items.answer: Train, bus or taxi — which one is right depends on your luggage and the hour.

items.when: My phone has a Korean number but Korean apps still reject me
items.answer: You do get an 010 number. What you do not get is Korean identity verification, and no tourist product at any price changes that.

items.when: I bought a train ticket and there is no gate to scan it at
items.answer: There is no gate. Walk to the platform and sit in your seat — that is the whole procedure.

items.when: I do not know what a subway ride or a taxi should cost
items.answer: A subway ride starts at ₩1,550 with a card and ₩1,650 without, and that gap repeats on every transfer.

groups.label: You cannot read what is in front of you

items.when: Every sign is in an alphabet I cannot read
items.answer: Hangul is not Chinese characters. Most people can sound out a sign after about ninety minutes.

items.when: I cannot tell what kind of restaurant this is from outside
items.answer: The last word on the sign tells you what they cook. Learn six words and you can read the street.

items.when: I do not eat pork, and I cannot read the menu
items.answer: Pork and fish stock hide in things that do not look like they contain either. There is also an official list of restaurants that do not use them.

items.when: I do not know what to say when I walk into a shop
items.answer: About eight sentences cover almost everything, and one of them is just pointing.

items.when: I need a pharmacy and every door looks like an office
items.answer: Clinic signs run to a fixed formula — name, specialty, then 의원 or 병원. Korean law bars anyone who is not a licensed medical institution from using those words at all.

items.when: Half the signs end in the same syllable and I do not know why
items.answer: 방 just means room. Korea names a business after the room you do the thing in — singing room, sauna room, PC room.

items.when: Everyone is calling each other names the subtitles do not translate
items.answer: Oppa, hyung, unnie, noona say who is older and how close you are. Subtitles usually replace them with a name, which loses the whole point.

items.when: My card paid for dinner but the booking site declined it
items.answer: Shop terminals do not run 3D Secure; Korean online checkouts do, and a card that is not enrolled gets refused. One call to your issuer before you fly usually fixes it.

items.when: I am ill and I do not have an appointment
items.answer: You do not book anything. Walk into a neighbourhood clinic, wait about twenty minutes, collect your medicine downstairs.

items.when: I have broken my glasses
items.answer: Walk into an optician. About ten minutes, no appointment, and no eye doctor needed — the optician does the test.

items.when: I am worried I am being overcharged
items.answer: Here is what ordinary meals actually cost, so you can tell.

groups.label: You are about to do something that has a rule

items.when: Can I get fined for walking down a street and taking a photograph
items.answer: In one lane of Bukchon, yes — ₩100,000, outside 10:00–17:00, and it applies to visitors exactly as to Koreans.

items.when: I heard hanbok gets you in free — what counts as hanbok
items.answer: It does, at every palace. There are rules about what counts, and rental shops do not always tell you them.

items.when: I came for the Secret Garden and could not get in
items.answer: It is a separate ticket and a separate booking, and in spring and autumn it sells out in minutes.

items.when: There are five palaces and I have one day
items.answer: They are not interchangeable. One of the five things on most lists is not a palace at all.

items.when: Someone asked how old I am in Korean age
items.answer: Korea changed to international age in June 2023. The answer is now just your age.

items.when: Am I paying for something that is free for me
items.answer: If you are 18 or under, or 65 or over, the royal palaces are free for foreign visitors too — and nobody tells you at the gate.

items.when: It is raining and I wanted to walk along the stream
items.answer: Cheonggyecheon runs below street level and closes on a published rainfall schedule. The spot your instinct picks — under a bridge — is where the sluice gates open.

items.when: I want to see my favourite group in Seoul but I cannot get near a ticket
items.answer: Speed is not the wall. The presale is a fanclub membership list, and the joining deadline can fall on the day the show is announced.
